captions.detailed: A road bike front fork assembly featuring a dark blue head tube segment, a black carbon crown, and twin black fork blades terminating in silver metal dropouts. A light grey alloy stem clamps onto the black curved drop handlebars at the top. The steerer tube passes through the head tube, establishing a revolute joint that allows the fork and handlebars to steer left and right relative to the frame.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a road bike front fork and handlebar assembly. It must feature a dark blue head tube segment, a black fork crown with twin blades and silver metal dropouts, and drop handlebars clamped by a grey alloy stem. Connect the fork and handlebars to the head tube using a revolute joint to enable steering.
captions.factory: Construct the model by defining three main parts: the fixed frame segment (head tube), the steering assembly (fork and handlebars), and the dropouts. Model the head tube using concentric cylinders. Build the fork crown using a box primitive, and extrude or sweep the blades and curved drop handlebars using wire paths or cylinders. Assemble the parts using a revolute joint centered along the steerer tube's vertical axis.
